purpose: Open work only: what is left, in what order, and the pre-registered acceptance test for each item. State, evidence ledger, venue metadata and closed gaps live in docs/audit/todo-history.md (sections 10-15).
recording_policy: Observations-only: write audit docs + todo.json + raw artifacts. Frozen CLAIMS.md / CONSOLIDATED_RESULTS.md / paper-A-final.* / tnnls_submission/** stay untouched without explicit user authorization.
decision_rule: An experiment runs only if it can change a claim's STATUS or a metric's MAGNITUDE. More seeds, more draws or a larger N on an already-measured effect do not qualify: they buy confidence, not strength, and the paper's weakness is not confidence. When a cell is power-limited or negative, stop measuring and strengthen the adapter: study the domain (the upstream implementation, the metric's own definition, the field's validity rules), write the design hypothesis down, change the code, then make ONE pre-registered measurement. Every experiment left in this file is either that confirmation run or a measurement defect that must be corrected.
research_protocol: 1) Read the upstream implementation of the state space being perturbed (channel geometry, latent geometry, embedding geometry) before proposing anything.
2) Read the metric's definition and the scorer, not just its name: what does it reward, and would it reward the change we are about to make for a trivial reason?
3) State the design hypothesis as a falsifiable sentence with the expected sign and rough size, in the audit doc, BEFORE touching code.
4) Change one mechanism at a time; keep the old arm runnable so the before/after is paired on the same seed and the same prior.
5) One confirmatory measurement at the cell's canonical N/NFE/seeds. No seed top-ups afterwards.
gate_note: The pytest entry is the fast canonical subset. Full pytest is run per change: 15 known failures (3 stale eval stubs; 12 order-dependent test_paper_metrics cases). docs-vs-code verifies 3370 claims since the 2026-10-21 archive move.
q1_gate: The paper's weakness is now a MECHANISM weakness, not a power weakness. Three fidelity cells regress (R5c production +9.5%, R5b CIFAR +52% at N=200, K7 novelty 12.6x down) and GAP-64 traced all three to one property of the blend: it shrinks variance. GAP-67 changes that property. If it works, the fidelity regressions become a solved mechanism; if it does not, the boundary is real and gets stated as one. Everything else in this file is either adapter work that follows from the same thesis, or a user-gated document step.

open_gaps.depends_on: none (GAP-73 and GAP-75 are done; the corrected R5c table is 9 regressions / 1 win / 2 ties)
open_gaps.est_wall: ~2 h code + ~1 h GPU (4 checkpoints x 1 arm, N=1000)
open_gaps.gap: The R5c fidelity cost is a MEAN shift, not a dispersion effect. Frechet decomposition at N=1000 (docs/audit/gap67-covariance-preservation.md section 2.1): production baseline (mean 4.881, cov 5.087) vs cosine (mean 5.641, cov 5.215) -- the mean term carries +0.760 of the +0.888 gap; w16e1_60k mean +1.480 of +1.758. The mean term increases on 4/4 checkpoints while the covariance term moves in both directions. GAP-67 falsified the dispersion explanation, so this is the only remaining mechanism for the fidelity cost, and nothing currently explains it.
open_gaps.design_hypothesis: The restart blends in noise that is independent of the prior, so the state at t=m is off the model's training manifold and the velocity field's conditional mean E[x1|x_m] is biased away from E[x1]. Two candidate forms: (i) a global DC offset (all 784 pixels shift the same way, e.g. a brightness/ink-mass bias) or (ii) a structured shift concentrated in the class-conditional means. Form (i) is correctable by a scalar; form (ii) is not.
open_gaps.research: (a) Compute the mean-shift vector delta_mu = mean_gen - mean_ref in pixel space and decompose it into its projection on the all-ones direction (DC) and the residual. (b) Check whether |delta_mu| grows with the number of restart rounds (per-round means are recoverable from a single run if the driver records them; otherwise instrument the driver additively). (c) Confirm the shift is not an artifact of the projection: the DC direction is not in the 128-d random projection's span unless the projection has a nonzero row sum -- check that first.
open_gaps.acceptance: (1) The DC fraction ||proj_DC delta_mu||^2 / ||delta_mu||^2 on 4 checkpoints x 2 arms. (2) |delta_mu| vs restart round. (3) Pre-registered: if the DC fraction is >= 0.5, a single scalar correction must recover >= 50% of the mean term; test it with one arm on production only. (4) If the DC fraction is < 0.2, the shift is structured and the gap closes as 'not fixable by a global correction'.
open_gaps.agent_action: 1) Write tools/gap72_r5c_mean_shift.py (reads frozen npz, no GPU for steps 1-2). 2) Run the decomposition. 3) Only if the DC fraction warrants it, add an opt-in mean-correction arm and run production. 4) Write docs/audit/gap72-r5c-mean-shift.md. 5) 6 gates + commit.
open_gaps.deliverable: Either a correctable mean artifact (which would turn R5c from a regression into a tie or a win) or a proof that the cost is structural.

open_gaps.depends_on: GAP-72 (the mean and variance channels must be separated before either is formalised)
open_gaps.gap: The surviving explanation for the rho contraction is the law of total variance: the restart injects independent noise at t=m and integrates to t=1, so the endpoint is approximately E[x1|x_m] rather than a draw from p(x1), and conditional means are under-dispersed. This is argued, not measured (docs/audit/gap67-covariance-preservation.md section 6.3). Separately, Theorem 5's variance term bounds the DEVIATION from the corrected prior, which is a different object from the MARGINAL dispersion measured by rho; GAP-67 measured that the marginal does not respond to the blend's second moment at all, so the two are decoupled and any paper sentence that conflates them is wrong.
open_gaps.design_hypothesis: The contraction is monotone in the injected noise fraction (1-m) at fixed restart time t0, and vanishes as m -> 1. The current design ties t0 = 1 - beta, so m and t0 cannot be varied independently; a fixed-t0 override is required to test this.
open_gaps.research: (a) The override must be additive and default-off so every frozen digest and D.4 vector is unchanged. (b) m -> 1 is the 'do not restart' arm; the prediction that the contraction vanishes there is nearly tautological, so the informative part is the SHAPE between m=0.2 and m=0.9, not the endpoint. (c) Any restatement of Theorem 5 is a paper-surface change and is out of scope here -- flag only.
open_gaps.acceptance: (1) rho contraction vs (1-m) at fixed t0 on production and w16e1_5k, 5 points. (2) Monotone within the bootstrap CI, or the explanation is falsified. (3) A one-paragraph mechanism statement written into the audit that distinguishes the deviation channel from the marginal channel, with the Theorem 5 flag.
open_gaps.agent_action: 1) Add a default-off restart_t0 override to the MNIST adapter. 2) Verify D.4 + the byte-identical control. 3) Run the 5-point sweep on 2 checkpoints. 4) Write docs/audit/gap74-conditional-mean-bound.md. 5) 6 gates + commit.
open_gaps.deliverable: The contraction stated as a measured mechanism rather than a conjecture, or falsified and replaced.

open_gaps.est_wall: ~1 day research + code; ~8 h GPU (N=1000, 3 seeds)
open_gaps.gap: R3 fg_dev is -0.061 with CI [-0.117,-0.001] but p=0.043 > the 0.00714 floor, on one seed. The adapter has three channels with incompatible geometry - coordinate (continuous, Euclidean), charge (6-valued, already has a categorical blend), raw_pair (5-class bond-type logits, CTMC) - and the restart blends all three with one scalar m. That is wrong twice over: interpolating a bond type produces a molecule that does not exist (half single, half double), and a blended coordinate with an unblended bond order is a geometry the velocity field was never trained on.
open_gaps.design_hypothesis: Per-channel m with a topology-locked schedule: the discrete bond channel keeps the prior's class (or resamples through the CTMC kernel) until the final round instead of being interpolated, and the coordinate weight is conditioned on whether the bond class changed this round. Use the existing adaptive_reflow/algorithm/per_channel_blender.py, which is implemented and has zero experimental use. Expected sign: fg_dev improves beyond the single-m arm, because the current arm is spending its restart budget producing off-manifold molecules.
open_gaps.research: (a) Read FlowMol3's CTMC sampler and the _solve_ode_upstream charge mapping to learn which channels are genuinely discrete. (b) Read the fg_dev scorer: does it reward fragment composition (topology) more than geometry? If so the bond channel is the lever. (c) Check whether bond orders are kekulized before scoring - if they are, aromatic/double interconversion is free and the topology-lock may be unnecessary. (d) The per-channel design must keep the total NFE fixed.
open_gaps.acceptance: (1) A per-channel arm and the current single-m arm on the same seeds and the same shared prior, N=1000, matched NFE. (2) Per-seed paired fg_dev delta with CI, then pooled 3 seeds (this is the confirmatory run the deferred GAP-62 would have been). (3) Pre-registered: SUPPORTED if the pooled CI excludes 0 and p < 0.00714; the per-channel arm must beat the single-m arm by >= 0.5 sd, otherwise record that channel geometry is not the bottleneck. (4) No seeds beyond 42/43/44.
open_gaps.agent_action: 1) Write docs/audit/gap68-flowmol3-channels.md with the hypothesis before coding. 2) Wire per_channel_blender into the FlowMol3 adapter behind a flag. 3) Verify default path byte-identical. 4) Run the two arms. 5) 6 gates + commit.
open_gaps.deliverable: R3 resolved as SUPPORTED or a bounded null with the channel hypothesis explicitly tested.

open_gaps.gap: R1's +74% hmmscan hits is the flagship positive, and its mechanism is a per-record RANDOM init (D-004b: init-only ~= full framework). That is a perturbation, not a design. Nothing in the adapter uses protein knowledge: the perturbation is isotropic over the ESM-2 embedding / sequence simplex, with no notion of conserved sites, family profiles, or foldability. GAP-60 showed the gain is not bought by diversity collapse, so the samples really are different - but we cannot say why, and a reviewer will ask.
open_gaps.design_hypothesis: Profile-aware perturbation, in two variants that share one control: (a) position-wise noise scaled by (1 - conservation), using the same Pfam HMM that the metric scores against, so the restart explores surface positions and leaves catalytic motifs alone; (b) perturb the ESM-2 embedding only and keep the sequence identity, so the fold is preserved while the surface changes. Expected sign: hits rise above the init-only arm, and the two variants separate - if (a) wins, the metric rewards motif preservation; if (b) wins, it rewards fold retention.
open_gaps.research: (a) How LineageFlow conditions on family - if family is already an input, the conservation weighting may be redundant and must be tested against it. (b) What hmmscan against Pfam actually rewards: recovery of known motifs (then (a)) or novel-but-plausible domains (then (b)). (c) The D-004b result means the comparison arm is init-only, NOT the plain baseline - beating the baseline again proves nothing new. (d) Reading the profile HMM per position costs a pass over the MSA; budget it.
open_gaps.acceptance: (1) Seed 42 first: profile-aware arm vs init-only arm vs baseline, N=1000, NFE=150, R=3, same prior. (2) Only if the profile-aware arm beats init-only by >= 15% with a CI excluding 0 do seeds 43/44 run (this is the confirmatory run the deferred GAP-59 would have been). (3) Pre-registered: SUPPORTED only if the gain over init-only holds at 3 seeds; otherwise R1 stays an empirical perturbation result and the paper says so.
open_gaps.agent_action: 1) Write docs/audit/gap69-lineageflow-profile.md with the hypothesis. 2) Read the Pfam HMM used by the scorer to get per-position conservation. 3) Implement both variants behind flags. 4) Run seed 42. 5) Escalate to 3 seeds only on the pre-registered condition. 6) 6 gates + commit.
open_gaps.deliverable: R1 either becomes a designed mechanism that can be described in one sentence, or it stays an empirical perturbation result with the boundary stated.

open_gaps.gap: Two fidelity regressions live in image domains (R5c production +9.5%, R5b CIFAR +52.33% at N=200), and the image adapters do nothing domain-specific: the blend is per-pixel, so it shrinks high-frequency content - where the model does its generative work - exactly as much as low-frequency content, where the prior is genuinely informative. GAP-64's rho explains the sign of the regression but not why the magnitude differs by checkpoint; the band structure is the obvious missing variable. The +52.33% is also an N=200 number that the project's own calibration says is inflated 40-65%, so the baseline must be re-measured before any arm is compared to it.
open_gaps.design_hypothesis: Spectral-aware blend: apply m per band in a DCT or wavelet decomposition, keeping the prior in low bands (structure) and the fresh sample in high bands (texture). Expected sign: the R5b and R5c regressions shrink by at least half relative to the pixel-space arm, because the shrinkage is applied where it is harmless.
open_gaps.research: (a) The CIFAR RF adapter's state space - pixel or latent; a latent blend makes the band argument different. (b) Whether Inception features are dominated by low-frequency content; if they are, the high-band preservation will not move FID and the hypothesis is wrong for a measurable reason. (c) The MNIST projection FID's basis, since R5c uses a projection rather than Inception.
open_gaps.acceptance: (1) FIRST re-measure the CURRENT arm at matched total NFE and N=1000 x 3: this is the retraction baseline that GAP-66 and GAP-63 were opened for, and it is run once, here, as the before. Pre-registered: if the matched-budget N=1000 delta is below +5%, the +18..+23% and +52.33% figures are retracted. (2) THEN the spectral arm on the same cells and seeds. (3) Pre-registered: the spectral arm must cut the regression by at least half; if it does not, the band structure is not the missing variable and the boundary is stated without it.
open_gaps.agent_action: 1) Write docs/audit/gap71-image-spectral.md with the hypothesis. 2) Locate the Wave 280 CIFAR driver and the R5c MNIST driver; add the matched-NFE constraint to the CIFAR driver (GAP-55 fixed MNIST, not CIFAR). 3) Run the before arm. 4) Implement the band blend. 5) Run the after arm. 6) 6 gates + commit.
open_gaps.deliverable: R5b and R5c either become non-regressions, or the image boundary is stated with a tested mechanism and a retracted magnitude.

open_gaps.gap: K7 is the least explained number in the paper: 12.6x less novel (3.7% vs 46.6%, McNemar p=1e-102). GAP-60 showed it is not a diversity collapse - within-generation clustering is unchanged - so the samples are diverse but all close to KNOWN Pfam families. Kanzi's state is a 64x64 continuous latent with an autoregressive decoder prior, and the blend treats all 4096 coordinates alike. A scalar blend in that space is a global push toward the decoder's high-likelihood region, which is exactly the behaviour K7 measures.
open_gaps.design_hypothesis: Decoder-aware latent blend: apply the GAP-67 covariance-preserving rescaling in latent space and, in addition, blend only the latent tokens whose decoded contribution is below a threshold (estimated by masking), leaving the tokens that carry sequence identity fresh. Expected sign: validity stays at or above the current arm while the novelty drop shrinks from 12.6x toward <= 2x.
open_gaps.research: (a) The inverse-projection bridge (kanzi-inv-proj-bridge follow-up): how a latent maps back to a sequence, and whether any latent direction is identifiable as 'identity'. (b) Kanzi's AR decoder prior: is it conditioned on the latent prefix? If so, a token-level blend changes the decoding order's meaning. (c) K7's novelty is measured against the 63.8M pfam_canonical build on different samples from R1 - the comparison must be run on the same samples as the validity number.
open_gaps.acceptance: (1) Validity and novelty measured on the SAME samples, same seeds, N=1000. (2) Pre-registered: the adapter is SUPPORTED if validity does not fall and the novelty drop is <= 2x; if the novelty drop is unchanged, the decoder prior is not the lever and K7 stays an unexplained boundary. (3) The powered validity test is GAP-47's run and happens after this lands, on these samples.
open_gaps.agent_action: 1) Write docs/audit/gap70-kanzi-latent.md with the hypothesis. 2) Read the inverse-projection bridge and the decoder prior. 3) Implement the token-selective blend behind a flag. 4) Run validity + novelty on the same samples. 5) 6 gates + commit.
open_gaps.deliverable: K1 and K7 become one trade-off curve, or K7 is stated as an unexplained boundary with the latent hypothesis excluded.
